title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: CLAUDE CODE 2.1.273 FIXES THE EXACT MANAGED-MCP CONTROLS THIS REPORT HAS DEFERRED TWELVE TIMES — THEY WERE BEING SILENTLY IGNORED, SO WRITING THEM ON ANY OF THOSE TWELVE DAYS WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED
bullets.summary: Archive grep on 2.1.273, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, disableClaudeAiConnectors, CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS, scheduled_tasks.json, advisor-tool, context meter: zero hits, all of them. The release states: 'Fixed allowManagedMcpServersOnly, deniedMcpServers and disableClaudeAiConnectors set via MDM or managed-settings.json being ignored when server-managed settings are also present.' Four further items land on our own failure modes: the context meter and auto-compact counting advisor-tool turns at roughly twice their real size, firing auto-compact at about half the real window; scheduled tasks running in the wrong session after .claude/scheduled_tasks.json was copied into another folder; sub-agents and background agents reported as failed with results never delivered; and a repository-chosen memory directory no longer loaded into the prompt under permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories. New config surface: CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS=1.
bullets.how: YES — and it reverses the meaning of standing action (b). Twelve fires recorded (b) as five cheap lines we kept failing to type, each drawing the same moral about our follow-through. The vendor now says three of the four controls did not take effect when server-managed settings are also present, which is our configuration: the lines were not cheap-and-deferred, they were cheap-and-inert. Two consequences pointing opposite ways. The self-criticism was mis-aimed; and the blocker is gone as of this release, so (b) is a genuine five-line write with a working target for the first time since 29 July. The auto-compact double-count is the quietly important fix: reconcile-before-building exists in our skill corpus specifically because compaction silently drops record of completed work, and the vendor has just said compaction fired at roughly half the real window. A skill written to survive a bug may be a workaround for something now fixed — worth a re-test before a rewrite.

bullets.title: CORRECTION, OURS: YESTERDAY'S THIRD FIRE REPORTED MONDAY'S TAPE AS TUESDAY'S AND CALLED THE REPEAT A TREND — TUESDAY CLOSED AT ROUGHLY A QUARTER OF THE MOVE WE PRINTED
bullets.summary: Archive grep on 13.85 and 'record close': hits in exactly one file, 2026-09-15.md, and in latest.json — the error is ours, one day old, and live on the dashboard now. Yesterday read 'Tuesday's tape: CrowdStrike +13.85% to a record close, Palo Alto +13.09%, Fortinet +9.04%, Zscaler +8.4%.' Those are Monday 14 September's numbers. Tuesday 15 September actually closed: CrowdStrike +3.02% to $242.49, Okta +2.15%, Zscaler +1.13%, Palo Alto +0.31% to $375.09, CIBR +0.95%, against QQQ -0.65% and the S&P 500 -0.31% at 7,607.40. No record close; Palo Alto, printed at +13.09%, finished at +0.31% — the headline calls it 'barely budges.'
bullets.how: YES, and the most useful thing in today's file. (a) The claim is falsified: two identical sessions were one session counted twice, so 'a position being taken' rested on duplicated data; the honest description of Tuesday is deceleration to about a quarter of Monday's thrust, narrowed to one name. (b) The underlying finding survives on better evidence than the percentages we got wrong: CIBR closed up while QQQ closed down — money rotating into security while the NASDAQ 100 softens, a rare pairing. (c) The best PRAGMA citation of the week is not a price at all but CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz on the Q2 FY2027 call: 'I think the AIDR business can be bigger than the EDR business, just given the pure number of agents which each person will have, which is estimated to be about 90.' AIDR ending ARR nearly tripled QoQ; record net-new ARR $333M, +51% YoY. Method consequence: extend the 15 Sep intake rule — a price is a dated observation, so a quoted move must carry the session it closed in, read at the page, or it does not get printed.

bullets.title: THE FIRST MACRO DEADLINE THIS REPORT HAS EVER CARRIED LANDS SIX HOURS AFTER THIS FIRE, AND THE CONFOUND IT CREATES HAS TO BE RULED IN ADVANCE, NOT AFTER THE TAPE PRINTS
bullets.summary: The FOMC decision and Summary of Economic Projections land today, Wednesday 16 September at 14:00 ET, ~91% implied for a +25bp hike from 3.5-3.75%, the first hike since 2023. This fire publishes at ~06:00 ET, so everything in this file predates the event. Added to DATED DEADLINES yesterday as the list's first macro item.
bullets.how: YES. Yesterday predicted the confound precisely — if the hike lands as priced, the rotate-out-of-compute trade gets a second unrelated engine and the two become hard to separate. Today is the day to bind ourselves before the result can tempt us. The rule, set now: any move in the cyber-versus-semis spread today is attributed to the Fed by default; the AI-governance bid gets credit only for the residual, and only if CIBR-versus-QQQ holds direction across a session where rates did not move. Bullet 2 is the argument for writing that down in advance — a report that mis-attributed Monday to Tuesday inside twenty-four hours, with the archive on disk, will certainly mis-attribute the Fed to its own thesis if it decides after the fact. Second, on what we are for: today's decision changes the discount rate on every AI-capex thesis, every agent-platform valuation we track, and the timing of Anthropic's own S-1. Carrying the calendar is right; carrying it and then narrating the tape is how a scan turns into a newsletter. The FOMC stays on DATED DEADLINES as a cause, not as a recurring bullet.

bullets.title: NINTH AND TENTH MIS-ATTRIBUTED PACKAGE IN FOUR DAYS — AND THE MIRROR THAT WAS STALE YESTERDAY IS CURRENT TODAY WITH A HOLE IN IT WHERE 2.1.272 SHOULD BE
bullets.summary: (i) The search layer returned Anthropic's Commerce Agents blueprint as current news. It is 2 September 2026; archive grep on commerce-agent hits 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-14. Killed on prior coverage, twice over. (ii) It returned Claude for Financial Advisors as a 15 September item, sourced to a 15 September trade-press write-up of a 14 September announcement — yesterday's morning-fire lead. Killed. (iii) The Releasebot mirror, which on 15 Sep self-reported 'Last updated: Sep 12' and could therefore neither confirm nor refute anything, now self-reports 'Last updated: Sep 15' and carries 2.1.273 in full — but its version sequence runs 2.1.273, 2.1.271, 2.1.270, skipping 2.1.272 entirely, the release yesterday's fire confirmed at the vendor's own repository.
bullets.how: YES. The kills are routine now, which is the point — the claim-grep is doing its job on its second day and cost about a minute. The mirror is the finding. Yesterday we learned a stale mirror proves nothing; today the harder version: a mirror that has caught up can still be missing a release in the middle, so 'current' is not the same as 'complete.' A freshness check on an aggregator is necessary and insufficient — what it licenses is reading the page, not trusting the list. Both of today's Claude Code facts are quoted from the mirror and both name the vendor's own CHANGELOG.md as original source; the mirror is being used as a reader, not as an authority.

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS — DAY SIXTEEN, FIRST FIRE. ONE ITEM CHANGES STATUS FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE IT WAS OPENED, AND NOT BECAUSE WE TOUCHED IT
bullets.summary: STATUS CHANGE: (b) the four managed-MCP controls — THIRTEENTH asking, but reclassified from deferred to inert-until-now; 2.1.273 fixes it, so it is a real writable five-line change with a working target. CONFIG (unwritten): omitClaudeMd — fourth naming, one frontmatter line, still untyped; maxEffortLevel; --system-prompt-snapshot off; CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS default; per-command allowed_domains; NEW CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS=1 (logged, not recommended — no gateway in our path). NEW RE-TEST: whether reconcile-before-building is still load-bearing now the advisor-turn double-count is fixed. ARTIFACT: (a) incident log six rows still prose, and bullet 2 is a seventh row that belongs in it; (c) skill-corpus audit — three instruments, zero runs, seventeenth day; (f) one creative-ops MCP behind graphic-designer — 64 days, unblocked since 15 Sep, unmoved. READ: RFC 9449, RFC 8707, body of arXiv 2609.00006. CARRIED: OPENROUTER_MODEL=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash (rerouted 04:00 UTC 14 Sep, still unread); which dsh / ls ~/.dsh; the launchd seam. DEADLINES: FOMC today 14:00 ET, Sonar 27 Sep, Docusign MCP GA 30 Sep, client-cert 17 Nov, DCR removal after summer 2027. KILLED ON PRIOR COVERAGE: Commerce Agents blueprint; Claude for Financial Advisors re-served. KILLED ON DATELINE: Fund Recs Agentic Platform + AI Ops (MCP-based, three production agents, zero archive hits, but only 'week of 13 September' resolvable and no dateline at the page). EMPTY, REPORTED EMPTY: frontier models — nothing dated 15-16 Sep, the September cluster was 1-10 Sep and is covered or killed; funding thin — Starroad $10M+ Series A+ and Yoom ¥700M, both 15 Sep, neither agent-platform; arXiv — nothing newer than 2609.10132 (9 Sep), fifth consecutive fire empty.
bullets.how: YES — the composition is again the finding, but it changed shape: for three fires running everything that moved was moved by somebody else; today something moved for us, and it moved by correcting a twelve-day self-criticism that was pointed at the wrong target.

praxis_lesson: WE SPENT TWELVE DAYS BLAMING OUR DISCIPLINE FOR AN ITEM THE VENDOR HAD BROKEN, AND ONE DAY MANUFACTURING A TREND OUT OF A NUMBER WE COPIED TWICE — THE SAME ROOT CAUSE, POINTED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Standing action (b) has been written up twelve times as five cheap lines we kept failing to type, each write-up drawing the same moral about our follow-through. 2.1.273 says three of those four controls were ignored when server-managed settings are also present, which is our configuration — so the lines were not cheap-and-deferred, they were cheap-and-inert, and every one of those twelve morals was aimed at us for something happening upstream. That is the flattering half. The unflattering half is bullet 2: yesterday's third fire printed Monday's session as Tuesday's, called the duplicate 'a position being taken,' and shipped it to the live dashboard, where it still sits. Palo Alto was printed at +13.09% and closed at +0.31%. Both failures are the same failure — asserting a cause without checking the record that was already on disk. In one direction we assumed the fault was ours; in the other we assumed the confirmation was real. The archive falsified the second inside twenty-four hours and the changelog falsified the first inside twelve days, and in both cases the evidence sat in a file we already had. The rule that generalises, extending rather than replacing the 15 Sep intake rule: a date must be read at the page, and so must a session — a price without the session it closed in is not data, it is a headline. SECOND, THE ONE TO ACT ON BEFORE THE FED PRINTS AT 14:00: the confound rule in bullet 3 is worth more than any bullet in this file, because it is the first thing this report has ever committed to in advance of the evidence; everything else here is retrospective. THIRD, AND NO LONGER A COMPLAINT ABOUT DISCIPLINE: omitClaudeMd is at its fourth naming and one frontmatter line; (f) is at 64 days and unblocked; (c) has three instruments and zero runs on day seventeen. Bullet 1 removed the excuse for (b) — it did not supply one for the rest. And the single most useful sentence produced by the whole ecosystem in the last forty-eight hours was not ours and not a changelog: a public-company CEO telling analysts that governing agents will be a bigger business than securing endpoints, because each person will run about ninety of them. That is the thesis PRAGMA sells, said out loud on an earnings call, and we found it while correcting our own error.
